rules.statement: The top-level port list must never depend on a parameter value.
CLK-type ports are free running, rising-edge active, with no clock gating inside the IP.

rules.condition: When an active-low reset is asserted
rules.statement: Active-low reset must stay low for at least one clock edge of its domain so the flops are reset; it is released synchronously outside the IP.

rules.condition: At each rising clock edge where the request is 1 and the acceptance condition holds
rules.statement: Each edge with request level 1 and acceptance condition true (not full / not empty) is exactly one transaction; request is level-sampled with no minimum width.
i_wr_data is captured only at the edge where the write is accepted and ignored otherwise.
LVL-STS flags are combinational from registers, stay 1 while the condition holds, and change only after a clock edge or synchronizer stage, except for static threshold effects.
REG-STS outputs are driven directly by a flop with no combinational logic and change only at a clock edge of their domain.

rules.condition: After a rejected write (while full) or read (while empty)
rules.statement: PULSE outputs are registered, 1 for exactly one clock cycle per event in the cycle after the rejected request, return to 0 by themselves, and are not sticky.
The consumer must sample PULSE outputs at every clock edge or count the cycles.

rules.condition: While the FIFO is in use
rules.statement: STATIC threshold inputs must not change while the FIFO is in use; they are written once before use, with no synchronizer.
The IP reacts to the i_rst_n_sw level sampled at i_clk_wr; one reset sequence runs per assertion and ends only after the level is de-asserted.
REG-LVL handshake signals come from flops, cross through a 1-bit synchronizer, change only on a handshake step and stay stable until the other side has answered.
Gray pointer registers change by at most one bit per clock edge and enter synchronizers directly with no logic before the first stage.
INT signals may be combinational or registered interconnect between two blocks.

rules.condition: From the cycle in which i_rst_n_sw is 0
rules.statement: Writes are blocked from the cycle in which i_rst_n_sw is 0; a one-cycle low pulse or a longer low level starts the reset handshake.
o_sw_rst_busy is set at the edge where the write FSM leaves RUN and cleared at the edge where it returns to RUN, equal to write FSM not in RUN.
o_full is combinational from the write pointer and synchronized read pointer; writes are rejected while it is 1, and it is 1 while the write side is blocked by software reset.
o_full_thr is a combinational function of i_full_thr and the pointers, 1 when occupancy estimate is greater than or equal to i_full_thr.
o_rd_data shows the word at the current read pointer (show-ahead); an accepted read consumes it and the next word appears.
o_empty is combinational from read pointer and synchronized write pointer, reads are rejected while it is 1, and it is 1 during the whole software reset.
o_empty_thr is a combinational function of i_empty_thr and the pointers, 1 when occupancy estimate is less than or equal to i_empty_thr.
o_mem_wr_en is 1 combinationally in the cycle when i_wr_en = 1 and o_full = 0.
The Gray pointer registers are updated only at the clock edge that accepts a write or read, respectively.
o_mem_wr_addr is a register output of the low bits of the binary write pointer, and o_mem_wr_data copies i_wr_data in the same cycle.
o_mem_rd_addr is a combinational function of i_rd_en and the empty flag, giving the low bits of the next read pointer.
The storage is read in every read-clock cycle with no read enable; i_mem_rd_data is valid after the edge that captured the address (latency 1) and drives o_rd_data.
The sync o_data is a register output delayed by S destination edges after the change (S to S+2 with the metastability model).
The cell resets or sets all stages asynchronously per PARA_AFIFO_CELL_RST_VAL; o_q is the last-stage output, or i_d itself with option 0.

rules.condition: At the i_clk_wr edge with i_wr_en = 1
rules.statement: The memory stores i_wr_data at i_wr_addr at the i_clk_wr edge when write enable is 1.
The memory samples i_rd_addr every read-clock cycle and o_rd_data registers the word at it with latency 1; the array has no reset.

rules.condition: At the rising edge of CLKW with WEB = 0
rules.statement: Each DW bit whose BWEB bit is 0 is written to the word at AW; the wrapper ties BWEB to zero for whole-word write.
At the CLKR rising edge with REB = 0, QR shows the word at AR after the edge; QR keeps its value while REB = 1.
i_rd_en_n of the RAM macro wrapper is tied to 0 by m_vlsit_afifo_mem.

rules.condition: Simultaneous read and write of the same address
rules.statement: The model VLSIT_CELL_SRAM_1W1R returns the old word and the stored word is not corrupted.
m_vlsit_afifo_ram_macro instantiates VLSIT_CELL_SRAM_1W1R as u_dont_touch_sram and nothing else, in every flow.
VLSIT_CELL_SRAM_1W1R is a synthesizable RTL model with the write port in the CLKW domain with mask BWEB and QR a CLKR-domain register.
